clue.text: A Lisbon banker taking ticket to US

parts.note: a tag is a label or ticket tied to something
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Portuguese bank official is handed a ticket for a trip to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests money, but here it is something with banks: the river that reaches the sea at Lisbon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the river flowing through Lisbon, and a river has banks, so it is a 'banker'.

clue.text: Froggy sounding horse?

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that sounds like the next one when spoken

parts.note: the animal's name, said aloud, matches a word for a croaky voice

explanation.surface: A French-flavoured question about what noise a horse makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Froggy' looks like a nod to the French, but it means having a frog in the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a frog in their throat has a rough, croaking voice.

clue.text: He minds the proposal, and doesn't mind saying so

definitions.text: He minds the proposal, and doesn't mind saying so

parts.words: He minds the proposal, and doesn't mind saying so
parts.note: plays on two senses of mind: to dislike a motion put forward, and to be unbothered about speaking up against it

explanation.surface: A man who dislikes a suggestion is happy to voice his dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: One who raises an objection is a person who dislikes a proposal and says so openly.

clue.text: Gas explosion; great warmth of feeling enveloping the city

indicators.note: one piece wraps around the other, so the scrambled letters sit within the warmth word

parts.note: a glow is a feeling of warmth and contentment

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters of the word before are scattered

explanation.surface: A gas blast, and a city wrapped in a warm glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' turns GAS into ASG, which 'enveloping' puts inside GLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, on the Clyde.

clue.text: Put a line across the passage?

definitions.text: Put a line across the passage?

parts.words: Put a line across the passage?
parts.note: sounds like blocking a corridor, but means drawing a line through a piece of written text to delete it

explanation.surface: Someone barricades a corridor with a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking through a section of writing with a pen deletes it.

clue.text: Miserable cash, income low, company never gets a move on

definitions.note: a description of a person, standing for the noun naming such a person

indicators.note: read as 'in come': the following pieces come in, inside the jumbled letters
a miserable state is a wretched mess, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: With poor pay and low income, the firm never makes progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'income' is split as 'in come': LOW and CO go inside SACH, the jumble of CASH made by 'Miserable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dawdler or laggard is someone who is always slow and never hurries.

clue.text: A marine dive-bomber making a cutter take account

parts.note: a razor is a blade for shaving, a cutter
a bill is an account of money owed

explanation.surface: A military aircraft built to cut and bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive-bomber' suggests a warplane; it is a seabird that dives for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The razorbill is an auk, a seabird that plunges from the air into the sea after fish.

clue.text: A grating cross-examination

definitions.meaning: a grid or lattice of bars, as over a window or in a cooker
intensive questioning, as of a suspect by police

explanation.definitionFit: A grill is a metal lattice, and to grill someone is to interrogate them hard.

clue.text: Edith's cut down to make it fit the paper

indicators.note: the name is shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: the girl's name, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman named Edith is trimmed so she fits in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' removes the final H from EDITH; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise and trim copy so that it fits the space available in a newspaper is the job of an editor.

clue.text: Billets making NEWS?

definitions.meaning: lodgings, places where soldiers are housed
N, E, W and S are the four compass points, each a quarter of the compass

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' lodgings are their accommodation, and north, east, west and south are the four cardinal points dividing the compass.

clue.text: Repudiate the infernal world; reform now

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: Turn your back on hell and change your ways now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' turns NOW into OWN, which follows DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate someone is to renounce or cast them off.

clue.text: Morally-crooked although alive to the New Testament

parts.note: to be is to exist, to be alive
NT is the standard abbreviation for the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone corrupt, though still living by the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for corrupt or dishonest.

clue.text: If United Nations come to this it will be contrary to established views

definitions.text: If United Nations come to this it will be contrary to established views

parts.words: If United Nations come to this it will be contrary to established views
parts.note: UN, the abbreviation for United Nations, placed before the word sought makes a word meaning against accepted opinion, so the word sought means conforming to it

explanation.surface: A warning that the UN's stance may defy accepted opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United Nations' is UN; prefixing UN to the answer gives a word meaning nonconformist.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional, holding the generally accepted beliefs, is the sense the UN prefix negates.

clue.text: A pilot may have to study its detailed ins and outs

definitions.text: A pilot may have to study its detailed ins and outs

parts.words: A pilot may have to study its detailed ins and outs
parts.note: a harbour pilot guides ships, and 'ins and outs' are literally the flows of the sea coming in and going out

explanation.surface: An aviator pores over the fine details of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' suggests an aircraft, but a harbour pilot steers ships into port and needs the times of high and low water.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart listing the times of high and low water at a port, consulted by mariners.

clue.text: Defeating the enemy with Hugo, leader of youth

parts.note: Victor Hugo, the French novelist who wrote Les Miserables

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Beating the foe alongside Hugo, a head of a youth group.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumph is the outcome of beating an opponent.

clue.text: Poor tramline's ending?

definitions.note: a noun here, an end point such as the end of a line

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A badly-run tram line comes to its end.
explanation.walkthrough: The tram line suggests the word for the station at the end of the route, which is also what the anagram gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus or end point, where a transport line finishes, is also called this.

clue.text: It could cut the ground from under a teetotaller coming in jeer

definitions.text: It could cut the ground from under

indicators.note: the pieces come in, that is, are placed inside the word for jeer

parts.note: to mock is to jeer or ridicule
TT is the usual abbreviation for teetotal, one who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone undermines a non-drinker who comes in to be mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut the ground from under' sounds like undermining someone; here it is a tool literally breaking up soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A digging tool like a pickaxe with a broad blade, used for breaking up hard soil and roots.

clue.text: Noted ace wove an amusing little tale

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads, so the letters of the words before are interwoven into a new order

explanation.surface: A well-known expert spun a funny short story.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, entertaining account of a real incident told in conversation.

clue.text: Such black gloom across the sticks, we hear

definitions.text: Such black gloom across the sticks, we hear

parts.words: Such black gloom across the sticks, we hear
parts.note: the sticks sound like the Styx, the river of the Greek underworld, and the darkness beyond it gives an adjective for gloomy

explanation.surface: Rumour has it the countryside is plunged in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sticks' looks like slang for remote countryside; spoken, it is the Styx, the river crossed into Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Very dark and gloomy, like the realm of Hades beyond the river Styx.

clue.text: Decayed creed on the depths of hell

annotationWithheld.why: Decayed creed on the depths of hell: DECRE + PIT needs an anagram of 'creed', and the only indicator is 'Decayed', which is also the definition (one word doing two jobs)
annotationWithheld.clue: Decayed creed on the depths of hell

clue.text: A noble look

definitions.meaning: a member of the nobility, such as a duke or earl
to gaze closely or squint at something

explanation.definitionFit: A lord in the House of Lords holds this title, and to gaze intently is the verb sense.

clue.text: Send out some left-overs?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Distribute some scraps of leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: Remnants are the bits remaining, as in 'odds and ends'.

clue.text: Toff's first in, dressed up, but hasn't paid his bills

definitions.note: a description of a person, standing for the noun naming such a person

indicators.note: one letter goes in among the others
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: robed means dressed in a robe

indicators.note: the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A well-dressed aristocrat leads the way but owes money everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROBED into DEBOR; 'in' puts T (from 'Toff's first') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owes money is the person who has unpaid accounts.

clue.text: 5 who came together

parts.note: a group of five who arrived at the same time, that is, were born in one delivery

explanation.surface: Five people who arrived at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Quintuplets, five babies born at one birth, shortened.

clue.text: Some sort of case for investing one pound in an urn

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the urn word

parts.note: a vase is an urn-like vessel
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A kind of case for putting a pound coin into an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A small suitcase or travelling bag.

clue.text: Roving pleasure-seeker has a bad turn in extreme suffering

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the suffering word

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

indicators.note: to turn the word round is to read it backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wandering hedonist suffers a nasty bout of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes DAB from BAD; with A it goes inside GOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadder about town, one who flits from one amusement to the next.

clue.text: Cover for person with a dagger?

definitions.text: Cover for person with a dagger?

parts.words: Cover for person with a dagger?
parts.note: the garment that goes with the blade in that phrase

explanation.surface: Asking what disguise an armed assassin might wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless outer garment, paired with the dagger in the phrase for spy intrigue.

clue.text: A final tour of 18 holes or just a call at closing time

definitions.meaning: a golf round is a circuit of the 18 holes of a course, and this is the closing one
in a British pub the landlord calls for final orders of drinks before closing

explanation.definitionFit: The concluding golf circuit, and the final serving of drinks called for in a pub before it shuts.
